chapter: Russell's band, records and Armstrong in the studio
title: 'I Can't Give You Anything But Love' with no arrangement
summary: With no arrangement and a three-minute limit, the technicians held all the say and the whole session produced one side.

story.theme_name: In the studio: making records, then and now
story.community_name: Making records: studios, takes and the technology

blocks.x: Now, you said they had no arrangement or set routine for this "I Can't Give You Anything But Love," so they kept

Oh, no. There was no arrangement. I mean, there was nothing written out for it. They had no music whatsoever. The first thing, they had to get the time on the thing. It had to be under three minutes. So they had to figure how many choruses, how many interludes, bars you could put in there to fill out the time or something, and this-and-the-other. Time you'd get one thing straight, there'd be something else to figure out. I don't know, the big mechanical heads which were running the thing, they had all the say. We were just... The musicians, we were just there. We had nothing to say whatsoever. Just do as you're told. One of them things.
So you remember, then, that nothing more was accomplished that day than that one number.
That one number. That one side.
